questions.question:
According to Labour and Employment Statistics 2022, match the states in the first column with their rate of unemployment in the year 2020-21 given in the second column.

<div class="min-h-8 text-message flex w-full flex-col items-end gap-2 whitespace-normal break-words text-start [.text-message+&]:mt-5" data-message-author-role="assistant" data-messag

options.text: i) a, ii) c, iii) d, iv) b
i) d, ii) b, iii) c, iv) a
i) d, ii) c, iii) b, iv) a
i) b, ii) d, iii) a, iv) c

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**i) b, ii) d, iii) a, iv) c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kerala** had an unemployment rate of **10.1%** in the year 2020-21, reflecting high joblessness in the state.
 
• **Goa** experienced an unemployment rate of **10.5%** during the same period, indicating significant employment challenges.
 
• **Haryana** had a lower unemployment rate of **6.3%**, which was comparatively better among the listed states.
 
• **Uttarakhand** had an unemployment rate of **6.9%**, positioning it in the mid-range among the states mentioned.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Labour and Employment Statistics** report is a vital source of information on the employment and unemployment scenario in India, providing insights into the economic health of the states.
 
• **Unemployment rate** is defined as the percentage of the labor force that is jobless and actively seeking employment.
 
• The **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)** measures the proportion of the working-age population that is either working or actively looking for work.
 
• The **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** conducts periodic surveys to gather data on employment and unemployment, which is crucial for policy-making and economic planning.
 
• **Covid-19 pandemic** has significantly impacted employment rates across states, exacerbating joblessness and altering economic dynamics.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the 'Quit India Movement' launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1942**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on **8 August 1942**, during World War II, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• Gandhi delivered the iconic "Do or Die" speech at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• The movement is also known as the **August Kranti** or August Movement.
 
• The British responded with mass arrests and repression, detaining many leaders of the Indian National Congress without trial.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World War II Context**

 
 
• The Quit India Movement occurred during the turbulent times of World War II, when British resources were stretched thin.
 
• India's contribution to the British war effort was significant, which led to increasing demands for self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Arrest of Leaders**
 
 
• Following the launch of the movement, the British arrested nearly all leaders of the Indian National Congress, including Gandhi, Nehru, and Patel.
 
• This led to a leaderless movement, which saw widespread but uncoordinated protests across the country.
 
 
 
• **Public Response**
 
 
• Despite the lack of central leadership, the movement saw massive public participation, including strikes, protests, and acts of civil disobedience.
 
• The British government responded with severe repression, including police violence, mass detentions, and press censorship.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Independence**
 
 
• Though the Quit India Movement was ultimately suppressed, it significantly intensified the Indian struggle for independence.
 
• It demonstrated the Indian population's unified demand for freedom, which played a crucial role in the eventual British decision to leave India in 1947.

questions.question: In the case of reptiles, their heart is not properly divided in to four chambers i.e., it consists of two auricles and an incompletely divided ventricle. Which of the following is an example of a reptile having a four-chambered heart?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crocodiles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Crocodiles are unique among reptiles for having a fully divided four-chambered heart, similar to that of birds and mammals.
 
• This four-chambered heart includes two atria and two ventricles, ensuring complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
 
• The structure allows crocodiles to maintain a high metabolic rate, which is beneficial for their predatory lifestyle.
 
• The presence of a four-chambered heart in crocodiles is an evolutionary adaptation that supports their amphibious mode of life, allowing efficient respiration both in water and on land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reptilian Heart Structure:**

 
 
• Most reptiles typically have a three-chambered heart consisting of two atria and one ventricle, with some degree of ventricular septation.
 
• This partial separation allows for the mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, which is sufficient for their metabolic needs.
 
 
 
• **Double Circulation:**
 
 
• Double circulation refers to the separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood within the heart, which is a feature seen in crocodiles and is characteristic of a four-chambered heart.
 
• This system allows for more efficient oxygen delivery to the body tissues.
 
 
 
• **Evolutionary Significance:**
 
 
• The fully divided heart in crocodiles is considered an advanced evolutionary trait, providing a physiological advantage in terms of metabolic efficiency and thermoregulation.
 
• This adaptation is also seen in birds, which share a common ancestor with crocodiles.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Mammals and Birds:**
 
 
• Both mammals and birds possess a four-chambered heart, which evolved independently in these groups.
 
• The presence of a four-chambered heart in crocodiles is a case of convergent evolution, where similar traits evolve independently in different lineages.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Saluva dynasty of Vijayanagara empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narasimha Deva Raya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Narasimha Deva Raya** founded the Saluva dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• The Saluva dynasty was established around the late 15th century.
 
• Narasimha Deva Raya was a key figure in stabilizing the empire during a period of internal strife and external threats.
 
• He was succeeded by his son, Immadi Narasimha, who continued the legacy of the Saluva dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayanagara Empire**

 
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 AD by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of the Sangama dynasty.
 
• The empire is known for its patronage of art, architecture, and literature, as well as its military prowess.
 
• It played a crucial role in resisting the invasions of the Deccan Sultanates and preserving Hindu culture in South India.
 
 
 
• **Saluva Dynasty**
 
 
• The Saluva dynasty was the second ruling dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire, succeeding the Sangama dynasty.
 
• It marked a period of transition and consolidation within the empire.
 
 
 
• **Krishnadeva Raya**
 
 
• Krishnadeva Raya, a ruler from the Tuluva dynasty, is often considered the greatest ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• He reigned from 1509 to 1529 and expanded the empire to its zenith.
 
 
 
• **Decline of Vijayanagara Empire**
 
 
• The empire eventually declined after the Battle of Talikota in 1565, where it suffered a massive defeat against the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates.
 
• This marked the end of the dominance of the Vijayanagara Empire in South India.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms is primarily associated with Eastern India states like Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chhau** is a traditional dance form primarily associated with the Eastern Indian states of **Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal**.
 
• This dance form is known for its **vigorous martial movements** and **graceful choreography**.
 
• **Chhau** incorporates elements of **martial arts, acrobatics, and storytelling** from Indian mythology.
 
• It is performed during major festivals such as **Chaitra Parva** and **Durga Puja**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Chhau**:

 
 
• **Seraikella Chhau** from Jharkhand
 
• **Purulia Chhau** from West Bengal
 
• **Mayurbhanj Chhau** from Odisha
 
 
 
• **Costumes and Masks**:
 
 
• Chhau dancers often wear colorful costumes and intricate masks.
 
• The masks are particularly prominent in Purulia Chhau, adding to the visual storytelling.
 
 
 
• **Musical Instruments**:
 
 
• Traditional instruments like **dhol** (drum), **shehnai** (wind instrument), and **dhamsa** (large drum) accompany the dance.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition**:
 
 
• In 2010, Chhau dance was inscribed in the **UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**.

questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution of India provide for a parliamentary form of government at the Centre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 74 and 75**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 74 of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President.
 
• Article 75 specifies that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President, and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• These articles collectively establish the framework for the parliamentary system of government in India, where the executive authority is derived from and accountable to the legislature.
 
• The Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, the lower house of Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary System of Government:**

 
 
• In a parliamentary system, the executive branch derives its legitimacy from the legislature and is accountable to it.
 
• The head of state is different from the head of government.
 
 
 
• **Collective Responsibility:**
 
 
• The principle that the executive (Council of Ministers) is collectively responsible to the legislature (Lok Sabha).
 
• If the Lok Sabha passes a vote of no-confidence, the entire Council of Ministers must resign.
 
 
 
• **President's Role:**
 
 
• The President of India acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• This ensures that the real executive power is vested in the elected representatives of the people.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister's Role:**
 
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of the government and leads the executive branch.
 
• Plays a critical role in formulating and executing policies, and in maintaining the support of the majority in the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which of the following crops is grown in the Kharif season in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) Soybean**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Soybean** is a significant Kharif crop grown in India.
 
• Kharif season crops are typically sown at the beginning of the monsoon season, which usually starts in June.
 
• Soybeans is mainly cultivated in the states of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is sown with the onset of the monsoon and harvested in September-October.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif Crops:**

 
 
• Kharif crops are also known as monsoon crops as they depend on the southwest monsoon rains.
 
• Other examples of Kharif crops include rice, maize, millets (bajra and jowar), cotton, groundnut, and pulses like moong and urad.
 
 
 
• **Rabi Crops:**
 
 
• Rabi crops are sown in winter from October to December and harvested in summer from April to June.
 
• Examples include wheat, barley, mustard, sesame, and peas.
 
 
 
• **Climate and Soil:**
 
 
• Soyabean requires warm and humid conditions with temperatures ranging between 20°C to 30°C.
 
• Well-drained loamy or clayey soils are ideal for soybean cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance:**
 
 
• Soybean is a crucial crop for its oil and protein content, playing a vital role in the food and agriculture industry.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of soyabean in the world, contributing significantly to the agricultural GDP.

questions.question: Samrat Choudhary and Vijay Kumar Sinha became the Deputy Chief Minister of _______________ on 28 January 2024.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Samrat Choudhary and Vijay Kumar Sinha were appointed as the Deputy Chief Ministers of **Bihar** on 28 January 2024.
 
• This appointment marks a significant political event in the state of Bihar, influencing the political dynamics of the region.
 
• Both leaders have previously held significant positions within the state government and their elevation to Deputy Chief Ministers is seen as a strategic move by their party.
 
• The political climate in Bihar is known for its dynamic nature, with frequent changes in leadership and policy direction.
 
• The appointment is expected to impact the administration and governance, bringing new initiatives and policies to the forefront.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bihar Political Structure:**

 
 
• Bihar has a bicameral legislature consisting of the Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly) and the Vidhan Parishad (Legislative Council).
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the government, while the Governor is the ceremonial head of state.
 
• Deputy Chief Ministers play a crucial role in assisting the Chief Minister in governance and policy implementation.
 
 
 
• **Samrat Choudhary:**
 
 
• He has held various significant positions in the Bihar state government.
 
• Known for his administrative capabilities and political influence in the region.
 
 
 
• **Vijay Kumar Sinha:**
 
 
• He has served in different capacities in the state government, bringing experience and leadership to his new role.
 
• Instrumental in various legislative and policy-making processes within the state.
 
 
 
• **Bihar's Political Landscape:**
 
 
• Bihar has a vibrant and competitive political environment with multiple parties vying for power.
 
• The state has seen frequent changes in leadership and coalition governments.
 
• Policies and governance in Bihar are significantly influenced by caste dynamics and regional affiliations.

questions.question: Which of the following is the autobiography of Bhishma Sahni?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aaj ke Ateet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aaj ke Ateet** is the autobiography of **Bhishma Sahni**, a renowned Indian writer and playwright.
 
• Bhishma Sahni is widely celebrated for his contributions to Hindi literature, particularly for his novel **Tamas**, which depicts the violence and trauma of the partition of India.
 
• **Aaj ke Ateet** translates to **"Today's Past"**, offering a personal and historical insight into Sahni's life experiences.
 
• The autobiography sheds light on Sahni's literary journey, his ideological beliefs, and his engagement with the socio-political issues of his time.
 
• It is a significant work that helps readers understand the life and thoughts of one of India's literary stalwarts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhishma Sahni**:

 
 
• Born on August 8, 1915, in Rawalpindi, now in Pakistan.
 
• He was a prominent Hindi writer, playwright, and actor, contributing significantly to Indian literature.
 
• His notable works include **Tamas**, **Basanti**, and **Jharokhe**.
 
• He was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1975 and the Padma Bhushan in 1998.
 
 
 
• **Tamas**:
 
 
• A novel by Bhishma Sahni published in 1974, based on the partition of India in 1947.
 
• It was adapted into a television series directed by Govind Nihalani in 1986.
 
• The novel explores the communal violence and human suffering during the partition.
 
 
 
• **Hindi Literature**:
 
 
• It encompasses a rich tradition of poetry, fiction, and drama.
 
• Key figures include Premchand, Harivansh Rai Bachchan, and Mahadevi Verma.
 
• It addresses various themes such as social issues, patriotism, and human emotions.
 
 
 
• **Autobiography**:
 
 
• A literary genre where an individual writes about their own life.
 
• Provides personal insight and historical context.
 
• Famous autobiographies include **The Diary of a Young Girl** by Anne Frank and **Long Walk to Freedom** by Nelson Mandela.

questions.question: In which year was the Multi-dimensional Poverty Index launched in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Multi-dimensional Poverty Index (MPI) was **launched in India in 2021** to measure poverty in a holistic way beyond income-based assessments.
 
• The MPI considers multiple deprivations at the household level in education, health, and living standards.
 
• It is developed by the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The Indian version of MPI is aligned with the global MPI methodology but tailored to India's socio-economic context.
 
• The launch of MPI in 2021 was part of India's efforts to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 1: No Poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multi-dimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• The MPI identifies multiple deprivations at the household and individual level in health, education, and standard of living.
 
• It uses 10 indicators to measure poverty in three dimensions: education, health, and living standards.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The SDGs are a collection of 17 global goals set by the United Nations General Assembly in 2015 for the year 2030.
 
• They cover a broad range of social, economic, and environmental development issues.
 
 
 
• **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI):**
 
 
• OPHI is a research center within the Oxford Department of International Development at the University of Oxford.
 
• It aims to build and advance a more systematic methodological and economic framework for reducing multidimensional poverty.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP):**
 
 
• UNDP works in nearly 170 countries and territories, helping to achieve the eradication of poverty, and the reduction of inequalities and exclusion.
 
• It helps countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, and institutional capabilities.

questions.question: Valabhi type of Nagara temples are generally __________ in shape, with a roof that rises into a vaulted chamber.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Valabhi type of Nagara temples are characterized by their **rectangular shape**.
 
• These temples feature a roof that rises into a **vaulted chamber**.
 
• The architectural style is distinct within the Nagara temple architecture, which is prominent in northern India.
 
• The Valabhi type is one of several sub-styles within the broader Nagara architecture, each having unique structural elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagara Architecture**:

 
 
• A prominent temple architecture style in northern India characterized by its beehive-shaped tower called Shikhara.
 
• Often built on a raised platform called Jagati.
 
 
 
• **Sub-Styles of Nagara**:
 
 
• Rekha-Prasad: Features a linear tower.
 
• Phamsana: Characterized by a broader base and shorter height.
 
• Valabhi: Recognized by its rectangular shape with a vaulted roof.
 
 
 
• **Temple Components**:
 
 
• Garbhagriha: The innermost sanctum where the deity resides.
 
• Mandapa: The entrance hall.
 
 
 
• **Regional Variations**:
 
 
• The Nagara style varies significantly across different regions in terms of structural design and ornamentation.

questions.question: Who was the chairman of the drafting committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhimrao Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar was appointed as the Chairman of the **Drafting Committee** of the Indian Constituent Assembly.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the **framing of the Indian Constitution**, which was adopted on 26th January 1950.
 
• Ambedkar is often referred to as the **"Father of the Indian Constitution"** due to his significant contributions.
 
• The Drafting Committee was formed on **29th August 1947** and had a total of seven members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constituent Assembly of India:**

 
 
• It was established to draft the Constitution of India.
 
• The Assembly held its first meeting on **9th December 1946**.
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the **President** of the Assembly.
 
 
 
• **Drafting Committee:**
 
 
• Besides Dr. Ambedkar, other prominent members included **Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar** and **K. M. Munshi**.
 
• The Committee's task was to prepare a draft Constitution for India.
 
 
 
• **Adoption of the Constitution:**
 
 
• The Constitution was adopted on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• This day is celebrated as **Republic Day** in India.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• One of the key features of the Constitution, providing essential rights to all citizens.
 
• These include the right to equality, freedom, against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.

questions.question: The Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur iron ore belt lies in which of the following groups of states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh - Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt is one of the major iron ore belts in India.
 
• This belt primarily spans across the states of Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra.
 
• It is known for having rich deposits of high-grade hematite iron ore.
 
• Prominent mines in this region include Bailadila in Chhattisgarh and the mines in the Chandrapur district of Maharashtra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hematite Iron Ore**:

 
 
• Hematite ore is the most important industrial iron ore in terms of the quantity used.
 
• It has a high iron content, typically around 70% iron.
 
• This ore is primarily used in the production of steel.
 
 
 
• **Iron Ore Mining in India**:
 
 
• India is one of the leading producers of iron ore in the world.
 
• The major iron ore belts in India are Odisha-Jharkhand, Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur, Bellary-Chitradurga-Chikmagalur-Tumkur in Karnataka, and Maharashtra-Goa.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance**:
 
 
• Iron ore mining contributes significantly to the economy, especially in terms of exports and employment generation.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the industrial development of a country.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**:
 
 
• Iron ore mining can have significant environmental impacts, including deforestation, soil erosion, and pollution.
 
• Efforts are made to mitigate these impacts through sustainable mining practices and rehabilitation of mined areas.

questions.question: Which team won the Ultimate Kho-Kho League Season 2 event?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat Giants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gujarat Giants won the Ultimate Kho-Kho League Season 2 event.
 
• The Ultimate Kho-Kho League is a professional Kho-Kho league in India.
 
• The league aims to revive and promote the traditional Indian sport of Kho-Kho.
 
• The second season featured teams from various regions, competing at a high level.
 
• The Gujarat Giants emerged as the champions through their excellent performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kho-Kho:**

 
 
• Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian sport, known for its fast-paced and strategic gameplay.
 
• It involves two teams of twelve players each, with nine players on the field and three substitutes.
 
• The game is played on a rectangular field, where players chase and tag out opponents.
 
• It requires agility, speed, and teamwork.
 
 
 
• **Ultimate Kho-Kho League:**
 
 
• The league was launched to professionalize Kho-Kho and bring it to a larger audience.
 
• It features franchise-based teams representing different regions of India.
 
• The matches are broadcasted on various sports channels, increasing the sport's visibility.
 
• The league has helped in nurturing and identifying new talent in Kho-Kho.
 
 
 
• **Franchise System:**
 
 
• Similar to other sports leagues, the Ultimate Kho-Kho League follows a franchise model.
 
• Teams are owned by various stakeholders, including celebrities and business entities.
 
• This model helps in generating revenue and marketing the sport effectively.
 
 
 
• **Promotion of Indigenous Sports:**
 
 
• The league is part of a broader initiative to promote indigenous sports in India.
 
• Other traditional games like Kabaddi have also seen a resurgence through professional leagues.
 
• These efforts are crucial for preserving cultural heritage and providing opportunities for athletes.

questions.question: Article ________ A supplements the 11th fundamental duty of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 21**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 11th fundamental duty under Article 51A of the Indian Constitution was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act in 2002.
 
• It mandates parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the age of 6 and 14 years.
 
• This amendment also led to the incorporation of Article 21A, which guarantees the right to education for children in the specified age group.
 
• Article 51A lists the fundamental duties of Indian citizens, intending to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• These duties are outlined in Part IVA (Article 51A) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Initially, there were 10 fundamental duties, but the 86th Amendment added the 11th duty.
 
• The concept of fundamental duties is inspired by the Constitution of Russia (erstwhile Soviet Union).
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law but are considered essential for citizens.
 
 
 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002:**
 
 
• This amendment made three significant changes: introducing Article 21A, adding the 11th fundamental duty, and modifying Article 45.
 
• Article 21A makes education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• Article 45 was revised to focus on early childhood care and education for children below the age of six years.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education Act, 2009:**
 
 
• This Act operationalizes Article 21A of the Constitution.
 
• It mandates free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• The Act sets norms and standards for schools, ensuring a child-friendly and inclusive learning environment.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy:**
 
 
• These principles are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They guide the state in formulating and implementing policies and laws.
 
• Although non-justiciable, these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country.

questions.question: A person having stunted growth and discoloured hair is most probably suffering from ________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protein Deficiency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Protein deficiency can lead to stunted growth in children as protein is essential for the development and repair of body tissues.
 
• Discoloured hair, particularly a reddish-orange tinge, is a common symptom of severe protein deficiency, commonly referred to as Kwashiorkor.
 
• Kwashiorkor is more prevalent in areas with limited access to protein-rich foods, such as certain regions in Africa, Central America, and South Asia.
 
• Other symptoms of protein deficiency may include muscle wasting, edema, and an enlarged abdomen.
 
• A diet rich in legumes, nuts, dairy products, meat, and fish can help prevent protein deficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kwashiorkor**:

 
 
• A severe form of malnutrition caused by an inadequate intake of protein.
 
• Common in children in developing countries where diets are high in carbohydrates but low in protein.
 
• Symptoms include edema, irritability, ulcerating dermatoses, and an enlarged liver.
 
 
 
• **Marasmus**:
 
 
• Another form of severe malnutrition caused by an overall lack of calories and protein.
 
• Characterized by severe wasting of body fat and muscle, leading to a "skin and bones" appearance.
 
• Common among children in regions with food scarcity.
 
 
 
• **Essential Amino Acids**:
 
 
• Amino acids that the body cannot synthesize on its own and must be obtained from the diet.
 
• There are nine essential amino acids: histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine.
 
• They are crucial for protein synthesis and other metabolic processes.
 
 
 
• **Protein-Rich Foods**:
 
 
• Foods high in protein include meat, fish, eggs, dairy products, legumes, nuts, and seeds.
 
• Incorporating a variety of these foods can help ensure adequate protein intake.
 
• Plant-based proteins can be combined to provide all essential amino acids, such as rice and beans.

questions.question: Who among the following was the chief guest of India's first Republic Day in 1950?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sukarno**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sukarno** was the first President of Indonesia and a prominent leader in the struggle for Indonesian independence from Dutch colonial rule.
 
• He was invited as the **chief guest** for India's first Republic Day on **26th January 1950**.
 
• Sukarno's presence symbolized the solidarity and friendship between India and Indonesia, both of which were newly independent nations at the time.
 
• His attendance at the Republic Day celebration marked a significant moment in post-colonial international relations.
 
• The selection of Sukarno highlighted the importance of fostering diplomatic ties with countries in the Asian region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Republic Day of India**:

 
 
• It marks the date on which the Constitution of India came into effect on 26th January 1950, making India a sovereign, democratic, and republic state.
 
• The day is celebrated with a grand parade in New Delhi, showcasing India's cultural diversity and military prowess.
 
 
 
• **Sukarno's Contribution to Indonesia**:
 
 
• Sukarno played a pivotal role in the Indonesian National Revolution and became the first President of Indonesia, serving from 1945 to 1967.
 
• He was a key figure in the fight against Dutch colonial rule and led Indonesia's struggle for independence.
 
 
 
• **India-Indonesia Relations**:
 
 
• India and Indonesia share historical and cultural ties, with both countries being part of the Non-Aligned Movement during the Cold War.
 
• The bilateral relations have strengthened over the years with cooperation in various fields such as trade, defense, and cultural exchange.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Chief Guests at Republic Day**:
 
 
• Inviting a chief guest from another country is a tradition that underscores India's diplomatic outreach and international relations.
 
• The chief guest is usually a head of state or government, symbolizing the importance of the relationship between India and the guest's country.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian representative in modern Olympics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Norman Pritchard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Norman Pritchard** was the first Indian representative at the modern Olympics.
 
• He participated in the **1900 Paris Olympics**.
 
• Pritchard competed in **athletics**, specifically in sprinting events.
 
• He won **two silver medals** in the 200 meters and 200 meters hurdles events.
 
• Pritchard's participation marked India's debut in the Olympic Games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milkha Singh:**

 
 
• Also known as the "Flying Sikh," Milkha Singh was a renowned Indian sprinter.
 
• He represented India in the 1956, 1960, and 1964 Olympics.
 
• Milkha Singh's most notable Olympic performance was in the 400 meters final at the 1960 Rome Olympics, where he finished fourth.
 
 
 
• **KD Jadhav:**
 
 
• Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav was the first Indian athlete to win an individual Olympic medal.
 
• He won a bronze medal in wrestling at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics.
 
 
 
• **Nilima Ghose:**
 
 
• Nilima Ghose was the first Indian woman to participate in the Olympics.
 
• She competed in the 1952 Helsinki Olympics in athletics.
 
 
 
• **Olympic Games:**
 
 
• The modern Olympic Games are an international multi-sport event occurring every four years.
 
• The Games are governed by the International Olympic Committee (IOC).
 
• The first modern Olympics were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first Regional Rural Bank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prathma Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Prathma Bank** was the first Regional Rural Bank (RRB) established in India.
 
• It was set up on **2nd October 1975**, under the provisions of the RRB Act, 1976.
 
• Prathma Bank was sponsored by **Syndicate Bank**, one of the leading public sector banks.
 
• The bank operates primarily in the rural areas of Uttar Pradesh, with a focus on providing credit and financial services to the agrarian and rural sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)**

 
 
• RRBs were established to provide sufficient banking and credit facilities for agriculture and other rural sectors.
 
• They were created with a view to include rural areas into the economic mainstream by providing financial services.
 
• The RRB Act, 1976, which governs RRBs, aims to develop the rural economy by providing financial aid to small farmers, artisans, and agricultural laborers.
 
 
 
• **Syndicate Bank**
 
 
• Syndicate Bank was a major public sector bank in India before its merger with Canara Bank in 2020.
 
• It played a significant role in the establishment of the first RRB, Prathma Bank.
 
 
 
• **RRB Act, 1976**
 
 
• This act provides the legal framework for the establishment and functioning of RRBs in India.
 
• It mandates that RRBs should be jointly owned by the Central Government, the State Government, and the sponsoring public sector bank.
 
 
 
• **Current Status of RRBs**
 
 
• As of now, there are several RRBs operating across various states, contributing significantly to rural development and financial inclusion.
 
• These banks have been instrumental in the implementation of various government schemes aimed at rural and agricultural development.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: The elements that are liquid at room temperature (25°C) are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bromine and mercury**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bromine (Br)** and **mercury (Hg)** are the only two elements that are liquid at room temperature (25ºC).
 
• **Bromine** is a reddish-brown liquid and is the only non-metallic element that is liquid at room temperature.
 
• **Mercury** is a silvery liquid metal, known for its unique property of being liquid at room temperature.
 
• Both elements have significant industrial and scientific applications due to their unique physical properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Melting and Boiling Points:** Bromine melts at -7.2°C and boils at 58.8°C, while mercury melts at -38.83°C and boils at 356.7°C.
 
• **Density:** Bromine has a density of 3.1028 g/cm³, and mercury has a density of 13.534 g/cm³, making it one of the densest liquids.
 
• **Toxicity:** Both bromine and mercury are toxic and require careful handling. Mercury exposure can lead to mercury poisoning, while bromine can cause burns and respiratory issues.
 
• **Uses of Bromine:** Bromine is used in flame retardants, water purification, and as a reactant in organic synthesis.
 
• **Uses of Mercury:** Mercury is used in thermometers, barometers, fluorescent lamps, and amalgams for dental fillings, though its use has decreased due to toxicity concerns.

questions.question: Maitrak dynasty was founded in which part of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Maitrak dynasty was founded in the region of **Western India**.
 
• It primarily ruled over the area of **present-day Gujarat**.
 
• The capital of the Maitrak dynasty was at **Vallabhi**, which is located in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat.
 
• The Maitrakas were known for their contributions to art, culture, and learning during their reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vallabhi University**:

 
 
• The Maitrak dynasty established Vallabhi University, which became a renowned center of learning in ancient India.
 
• It was known for its studies in Buddhism, Jainism, and other Indian philosophies.
 
 
 
• **Founder of Maitrak Dynasty**:
 
 
• The Maitrak dynasty was founded by **Senapati Bhatarka** in the late 5th century.
 
• He was a general under the Gupta Empire before establishing his own kingdom.
 
 
 
• **Religious Influence**:
 
 
• The Maitrakas were patrons of both Hinduism and Buddhism.
 
• They built several temples and stupas, promoting religious harmony.
 
 
 
• **End of the Dynasty**:
 
 
• The Maitrak dynasty came to an end in the 8th century due to invasions by the Arabs.
 
• The last ruler of the dynasty was Siladitya VI.

questions.question: Sonu Nigam was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for which of the following fields?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Art**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sonu Nigam is a renowned Indian playback singer, live performer, composer, and actor who has sung in multiple languages, including Hindi, Kannada, and Bengali.
 
• He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022, which is the fourth highest civilian award in India, for his contributions to the field of Art.
 
• Sonu Nigam has received numerous accolades for his singing, including National Film Awards, Filmfare Awards, and state awards.
 
• His versatile voice has made him one of the most popular and respected playback singers in the Indian music industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards:**

 
 
• The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors in India, instituted in 1954. They are announced annually on Republic Day.
 
• The awards are given in three categories: Padma Vibhushan (for exceptional and distinguished service), Padma Bhushan (distinguished service of a high order), and Padma Shri (distinguished service).
 
 
 
• **Playback Singing:**
 
 
• Playback singing is the recording of songs by singers for use in films, where the actors lip-sync to the pre-recorded tracks.
 
• It is a common practice in Indian cinema, with playback singers often gaining significant popularity.
 
 
 
• **National Film Awards:**
 
 
• The National Film Awards is the most prominent film award ceremony in India, established in 1954. It is administered by the Directorate of Film Festivals, an organization set up by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
 
• These awards aim to encourage the production of films of high aesthetic and technical standard and educational and cultural value.
 
 
 
• **Versatility in Singing:**
 
 
• Versatile singers, like Sonu Nigam, are known for their ability to sing in various genres and languages, showcasing their adaptability and talent.
 
• This versatility contributes significantly to their popularity and longevity in the music industry.

questions.question: For transporting water from one place to another, some man-made structures used to distribute water to a place far away are known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**aqueducts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aqueducts** are man-made structures designed for transporting water from one location to another.
 
• They have been used since ancient times, with famous examples such as the Roman aqueducts that supplied water to cities and towns.
 
• Aqueducts can be constructed as bridges across valleys or as tunnels through hills, depending on the terrain.
 
• They are often built from durable materials such as stone, concrete, and steel to ensure long-term functionality and stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of Aqueducts**:

 
 
• The concept of aqueducts dates back to ancient civilizations, including the Greeks, Egyptians, and Romans.
 
• The Roman aqueducts are among the most renowned, with some still in use today, showcasing their advanced engineering techniques.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of Aqueducts**:
 
 
• Aqueducts were primarily built to supply water for drinking, irrigation, and public baths.
 
• They also played a crucial role in maintaining sanitation and public health in ancient cities.
 
 
 
• **Modern Aqueducts**:
 
 
• In contemporary times, aqueducts continue to be essential for urban water supply systems.
 
• Modern engineering advancements have allowed for more efficient and large-scale aqueduct projects.
 
 
 
• **Famous Examples**:
 
 
• The Pont du Gard in France is an iconic Roman aqueduct bridge.
 
• The California Aqueduct in the United States is a major infrastructure project that transports water across the state.
